- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price declines, model frequently undercorrects; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently overestimates in early periods of a downward trend (e.g., after sentiment drop); apply lagged mean reversion: subtract 1–2% of prior period’s forecast if sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment change is negative and news volume drops to 0, model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict in high-sentiment periods; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per unit of sentiment above 0.67.
